def-arbitrary-rank-coxeter-system-and-br:
## Definition

Let $S$ be any set, possibly infinite, and let $m:S\times S\to\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a Coxeter matrix: $m(s,s)=1$, and for distinct $s,t$, $m(s,t)=m(t,s)\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$. Let $F(S)$ be the free group on $S$, let $N$ be the normal closure of
$$
\{s^2:s\in S\}\cup\{(st)^{m(s,t)}:s\ne t,\ m(s,t)<\infty\},
$$
and define $W=F(S)/N$. The image of $s\in S$ in $W$ is also denoted $s$. This is the Coxeter group presented by $(S,m)$.

For $w\in W$, define its length by
$$
\ell(w)=\min\{k\in\mathbb N: w=s_1\cdots s_k\text{ for some }s_1,\ldots,s_k\in S\}.
$$
The set is nonempty because every element of the quotient has a finite word in $S\cup S^{-1}$ and the relators give $s^{-1}=s$; its minimum exists by the well-ordering principle. A word of length $\ell(w)$ for $w$ is a reduced expression; the empty word is the reduced expression of $1$.

Define the reflection set $T=\{x s x^{-1}:x\in W,\ s\in S\}$. Write $u\to v$ if $v=ut$ for a reflection $t\in T$ and $\ell(v)>\ell(u)$. Define the reflection-chain Bruhat order by $u\le v$ if there is a finite chain $u=u_0\to u_1\to\cdots\to u_k=v$; the empty chain is allowed. Length strictly increases on each nonempty chain, so this relation is a partial order. The exact reduced-subword description and finite-interval consequence needed below are established in [[thm-arbitrary-rank-finite-parabolics-and-bruhat-subword]].

When $S$ is finite, the presentation and length agree with [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], and the reflection-chain order agrees with [[def-cg-bruhat-order-by-reflection-chains]]. No exchange, standard-parabolic, reduced-subword, or interval-finiteness property is included in this definition; those properties are justified separately.
def-canonical-basic-set-for-hecke-specia:
## Definition

Let $O$ be a Noetherian commutative local domain, with fraction field $K$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k_0=O/\mathfrak m$. Allow a specified field extension $k/k_0$ as the specialization field. The nonfield DVR case is included: a nonfield discrete valuation ring is equivalently a local PID with nonzero maximal ideal ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]]); the original residue-field specialization is $k=k_0$. Let $H_O$ be a finite free $O$-algebra, so it has finite rank as an $O$-module. Assume the generic algebra $H_K=K\otimes_O H_O$ is split semisimple, meaning a finite product of full matrix algebras over $K$; assume $H_k=k\otimes_O H_O$ is split, meaning each simple module remains simple after extending the field. A simple module is a nonzero module with no proper nonzero submodule. Write $\operatorname{Irr}(H_K)$ and $\operatorname{Irr}(H_k)$ for their isomorphism classes of simple modules. For each $E\in\operatorname{Irr}(H_K)$, choose an $H_O$-stable $O$-lattice $\Lambda_E\subset E$, meaning a finite free $O$-submodule spanning $E$ over $K$. Assume each simple $M\in\operatorname{Irr}(H_k)$ occurs in at least one reduction $k\otimes_{k_0}(\Lambda_E/\mathfrak m\Lambda_E)$, so every column below is nonzero. For such $M$, let
$$
d_{E,M}=[k\otimes_{k_0}(\Lambda_E/\mathfrak m\Lambda_E):M]
$$
be the multiplicity of $M$ among the composition factors of this finite-dimensional $H_k$-module. A composition series is a finite strict submodule chain with simple successive quotients; one exists by induction on module dimension, and Jordan–Hölder makes its multiplicities independent of the chosen series ([[def-composition-series-and-composition-factors-of-an-object]], [[thm-jordan-holder-theorem-in-an-abelian-category]]). The matrix $D=(d_{E,M})$ is the decomposition matrix for these chosen lattices. This definition makes no choice-independence assertion for arbitrary local orders. The finite-Weyl theorem below supplies free integral models and proves their multiplicities independent in its complete local setting; the rank-one worked specialization gives its lattices directly.

Fix an integer-valued statistic $\alpha_E$ on $\operatorname{Irr}(H_K)$. In Geck's finite-Weyl Hecke convention this is the Schur-element exponent denoted $\alpha_E$; its particular values do not enter the identity-matrix case. Put
$$
\check\alpha_M=\min\{\alpha_E:d_{E,M}>0\}.
$$
A subset $B\subseteq\operatorname{Irr}(H_K)$ is a **canonical basic set** (relative to $D$ and $\alpha$) if there is a bijection $M\mapsto E(M)$ from $\operatorname{Irr}(H_k)$ to $B$ satisfying
$$
d_{E(M),M}=1,\qquad \alpha_{E(M)}=\check\alpha_M,
$$
and, for every $E,M$,
$$
d_{E,M}>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \check\alpha_M<\alpha_E\ \text{or}\ E=E(M).
$$
This is a definition only; it makes no claim that such a subset exists in every specialization.
def-schur-elements-from-a-symmetrizing-t:
## Definition

Let $K$ be a field and $H$ a finite-dimensional split semisimple $K$-algebra, meaning $H\cong\prod_{i=1}^n M_{d_i}(K)$ for positive integers $d_i$. Let $\tau:H\to K$ be a symmetrizing trace: $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$, and the bilinear form $(a,b)\mapsto\tau(ab)$ is nondegenerate. For each simple $H$-module $E$, let $\chi_E(h)=\operatorname{Tr}_K(h|_E)$ be its character. If the trace has an expansion
$$
\tau=\sum_{E\in\operatorname{Irr}(H)}c_E^{-1}\chi_E
$$
with all $c_E\in K^\times$, the scalars $c_E$ are the **Schur elements** of the pair $(H,\tau)$. The definition makes no existence claim for an arbitrary functional; existence and values require a separate proof in the specified regime. The rank-one specialization computes them directly, while the finite-Weyl asymptotic theorem proves the full trace expansion and its leading coefficients.

For the canonical finite Coxeter Hecke trace and its symmetric perfect pairing, see [[def-hh-canonical-hecke-trace-and-symmetrizing-form]] and [[thm-hh-canonical-hecke-trace-is-symmetric-and-perfect]].
lem-complete-local-hecke-modular-systems:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$ and let $\theta:A\to k$ be a unital homomorphism to a field. Set $\mathfrak p=\ker\theta$, $k_0=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)\subseteq k$, and let $R$ be the maximal-adic completion of $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $R$ is a complete separated Noetherian local domain with residue field $k_0$, and $A\to R$ is injective. Thus $\mathbb Q(v)$ embeds in $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$, and $A\to R\to k_0\to k$ equals $\theta$.

Every finite projective $R$-module is free, with equal fraction-field and residue-field dimensions. In every finite associative unital $R$-algebra $C$, every idempotent of $C/\mathfrak m_R C$ lifts to an idempotent of $C$. For any right $C$-module, multiplication by such an idempotent is an exact projection commuting with scalar extension. In particular, a filtration with finite free layers remains exact on its projected layers after passing to $F$ or $k_0$. If $J_R=\bigoplus_E M_{d_E}(R)$, every $R$-finite-free $J_R$-module has the same simple multiplicities in its generic and residue fibres.
def-unequal-parameter-weight-function-an:
## Definition

Let $(W,S)$ be as in [[def-arbitrary-rank-coxeter-system-and-bruhat-order]]. A **totally ordered abelian group** $(\Gamma,+,0,<)$ is an abelian group with a total order invariant under translation. Its group algebra $A=\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$ consists of finite sums $\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}a_\gamma v^\gamma$, where $a_\gamma\in\mathbb Z$, with $v^\gamma v^\delta=v^{\gamma+\delta}$. Define the ring involution $\overline{v^\gamma}=v^{-\gamma}$, and set
$$
A_{<0}=\bigoplus_{\gamma<0}\mathbb Z v^\gamma,\qquad A_{\le0}=\bigoplus_{\gamma\le0}\mathbb Z v^\gamma.
$$

A **weight function** is a map $L:W\to\Gamma$ such that $L(xy)=L(x)+L(y)$ whenever $\ell(xy)=\ell(x)+\ell(y)$. Its simple-generator parameters are $L(s)$ for $s\in S$. The exact criterion for prescribing those values on the simple generators is proved in [[lem-simple-generator-weights-extend-to-a-weight-function]]. No sign restriction on $L(s)$ is part of this definition.

The coefficient ordering used on the weighted Kazhdan–Lusztig basis is the given order on $\Gamma$, through $A_{<0}$. The group algebra elements $v^{L(s)}$ are units for every $s\in S$.
thm-arbitrary-rank-finite-parabolics-and:
## Statement

Let $S$ be any set with Coxeter matrix $m$, and let $W,\ell,T,\le$ be as in [[def-arbitrary-rank-coxeter-system-and-bruhat-order]]. For a finite $J\subseteq S$, let $W_J^*$ be the group presented by the restricted matrix $m|_J$, and let $\phi_J:W_J^*\to W$ send each generator to the same-named element.

1. The map $\phi_J$ is injective with image $\langle J\rangle$, and intrinsic length in $W_J^*$ equals ambient length in $W$ on this subgroup.
2. For $y,w\in W$, $y\le w$ if and only if a reduced expression of $y$ occurs as a subword of any fixed reduced expression of $w$. In particular, the interval $\{y:y\le w\}$ is finite and has at most $2^{\ell(w)}$ elements.
3. For every $s\in S$ and $w\in W$, $\ell(sw)=\ell(w)\pm1$ and $\ell(ws)=\ell(w)\pm1$.
lem-simple-generator-weights-extend-to-a:
## Statement

Let $S$ be any set with Coxeter matrix $m$, let $(W,S)$ be the presented system of [[def-arbitrary-rank-coxeter-system-and-bruhat-order]], and let $\Gamma$ be the ordered abelian group of [[def-unequal-parameter-weight-function-and-coefficient-order]]. Every weight function $L:W\to\Gamma$ has $L(s)=L(t)$ whenever $s\ne t$, $m(s,t)<\infty$, and $m(s,t)$ is odd. Conversely, every label map $\lambda:S\to\Gamma$ satisfying these odd-edge equalities extends uniquely to a weight function with $L(s)=\lambda(s)$.
def-unequal-parameter-coxeter-hecke-alge:
## Definition

Let $(W,S)$, $\Gamma$, $A=\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$, and $L:W\to\Gamma$ be as in [[def-arbitrary-rank-coxeter-system-and-bruhat-order]] and [[def-unequal-parameter-weight-function-and-coefficient-order]]. For $s\in S$, write $q_s=v^{L(s)}\in A^\times$. Let $F=A\langle T_s:s\in S\rangle$ be the free associative $A$-algebra and let $I$ be the two-sided ideal generated by
$$
(T_s-q_s)(T_s+q_s^{-1})\quad(s\in S)
$$
and, for each distinct $s,t\in S$ with finite $m(s,t)$, the equality of the two alternating products of $T_s,T_t$ having $m(s,t)$ factors. Define the **unequal-parameter Coxeter Hecke algebra** by $H_A(W,L)=F/I$, and use $T_s$ for the image of a generator. For $m(s,t)=\infty$ there is no braid relation between $T_s$ and $T_t$.

The quadratic relation is equivalently
$$
T_s^2=(q_s-q_s^{-1})T_s+1,
$$
so each $T_s$ is invertible with $T_s^{-1}=T_s-(q_s-q_s^{-1})$. The basis, bar, and Bruhat support properties are not part of this definition; they are proved in [[lem-unequal-parameter-hecke-standard-basis-and-bar-triangularity]].
lem-unequal-parameter-hecke-standard-bas:
## Statement

Let $S$ be any set with Coxeter group $W$, let $L:W\to\Gamma$ be a weight function as in [[def-unequal-parameter-weight-function-and-coefficient-order]], and let $H_A(W,L)$ be as in [[def-unequal-parameter-coxeter-hecke-algebra]]. Then:

1. For each $w$, the product $T_w$ along a reduced expression is independent of the chosen expression, and $\{T_w:w\in W\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_A(W,L)$.
2. The assignments $\overline{v^\gamma}=v^{-\gamma}$ and $\overline{T_s}=T_s^{-1}$ extend to an involutive semilinear algebra automorphism of $H_A(W,L)$.
3. For every reduced expression of $w$, the expansion of $\overline{T_w}-T_w$ in the standard basis is supported on $T_y$ with $y<w$ in Bruhat order.
thm-unequal-parameter-kazhdan-lusztig-ba:
## Statement

Let $S$ be any set with Coxeter group $W$, let $L:W\to\Gamma$ be any weight function into a totally ordered abelian group, let $A=\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$, and let $H_A(W,L)$ and its bar involution be as above. For each $w\in W$, there is a unique element $C_w\in H_A(W,L)$ such that
$$
\overline{C_w}=C_w,\qquad C_w=T_w+\sum_{y<w}p_{y,w}T_y,\qquad p_{y,w}\in A_{<0}.
$$
The family $\{C_w:w\in W\}$ is an $A$-basis. For a simple generator $s$ the normalization is
$$C_s=\begin{cases}T_s+v^{-L(s)},&L(s)>0,\\T_s,&L(s)=0,\\T_s-v^{L(s)},&L(s)<0.\end{cases}$$
def-unequal-parameter-cells-and-cell-quo:
## Definition

Let $C_w$ be the basis of [[thm-unequal-parameter-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. For $x,y\in W$, write $x\leftarrow_L y$ if the coefficient of $C_x$ in $C_sC_y$ is nonzero for some $s\in S$. Write $x\le_L y$ if there is a finite chain $x=w_0,\ldots,w_n=y$ with $w_i\leftarrow_L w_{i+1}$ at every step. Define $x\leftarrow_R y$ from the coefficient of $C_x$ in $C_yC_s$, and define $\le_R$ by finite chains of such steps. Define $x\le_{LR}y$ by finite chains in which each step is either a left or a right step. The length-zero chain makes each relation reflexive, and concatenation makes each transitive. Mutual comparability defines equivalence relations; their classes are the left, right, and two-sided **cells**.

For a left cell $\mathcal C$, define
$$I^L_{\le\mathcal C}=\operatorname{span}_A\{C_x:x\le_L y\text{ for some }y\in\mathcal C\},\qquad I^L_{<\mathcal C}=\operatorname{span}_A\{C_x:x\le_L y\text{ for some }y\in\mathcal C,\ x\notin\mathcal C\}.$$
Define $I^R_{\le\mathcal C}, I^R_{<\mathcal C}$ for a right cell and $I^{LR}_{\le\mathcal C}, I^{LR}_{<\mathcal C}$ for a two-sided cell in the same way, using the corresponding preorder. The associated left cell quotient, right cell quotient, and two-sided cell quotient are respectively $I^L_{\le\mathcal C}/I^L_{<\mathcal C}$, $I^R_{\le\mathcal C}/I^R_{<\mathcal C}$, and $I^{LR}_{\le\mathcal C}/I^{LR}_{<\mathcal C}$. [[thm-unequal-parameter-cell-quotients-are-modules]] proves that these quotients inherit the stated module or bimodule actions and have bases indexed by their cells.
def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data:
## Definition

Work in the **split generic finite-Weyl setting**: $W$ is a finite Weyl group, $L:W\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ is a weight function, $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$, and $H=H_A(W,L)$ has the symmetric normalization $(T_s-v^{L(s)})(T_s+v^{-L(s)})=0$. Its KL basis is $C_w$. Write $K=\mathbb Q(v)$ and assume the generic algebra $H_K$ is split semisimple, as in the generic setup of [[def-canonical-basic-set-for-hecke-specialization]]. This hypothesis supplies the generic labels; this item asserts no new theorem on generic rational splitting. Let $\tau(T_w)=\delta_{w,1}$ be the canonical symmetrizing trace.

The $A$-linear algebra involution $\dagger$ is $T_s\mapsto-T_s^{-1}$, and put $D_w=C_w^\dagger$. Define structure constants by $C_xC_y=\sum_z h_{x,y,z}C_z$; equivalently $D_xD_y=\sum_z h_{x,y,z}D_z$. Define

$$a(z)=\min\{n\ge0:v^n h_{x,y,z}\in\mathbb Z[v]\text{ for all }x,y\in W\},\qquad \gamma_{x,y,z}=[v^0](v^{a(z)}h_{x,y,z^{-1}}).$$

The integer $a(z)$ exists since $W$ is finite and all $h$ are Laurent polynomials invariant under bar. Let $\Delta(z)$ be the negative of the largest exponent in $\tau(C_z)$, and $n_z$ its nonzero coefficient. If $\tau(C_z)=0$, put $\Delta(z)=\infty$ and $n_z=0$. Let $\mathcal D=\{z:a(z)=\Delta(z)\}$. In particular $\Delta(1)=0$ and $n_1=1$; P3 below forces $a(1)=0$.

The following are **explicit hypotheses**, not assertions for every unequal weight. They are precisely the subset used in Geck section 5.2:

- P2: if $d\in\mathcal D$ and $\gamma_{x,y,d}\ne0$, then $x=y^{-1}$.
- P3: for every $y$ there is a unique $d\in\mathcal D$ with $\gamma_{y^{-1},y,d}\ne0$.
- P4: $h_{x,y,z}\ne0$ implies $a(z)\ge a(x)$ and $a(z)\ge a(y)$.
- P5: in P3, $\gamma_{y^{-1},y,d}=n_d=\pm1$.
- P6: every $d\in\mathcal D$ satisfies $d^2=1$.
- P7: $\gamma_{x,y,z}=\gamma_{y,z,x}$.
- P8: $\gamma_{x,y,z}\ne0$ implies $a(x)=a(y)=a(z)$.
- P15′: if $a(w)=a(y)$, then

$$\sum_u h_{x,u,y}\gamma_{w,x',u^{-1}}=\sum_u h_{x,w,u}\gamma_{u,x',y^{-1}}.$$

All sums are finite. These hypotheses produce the asymptotic algebra and modular theorem in the following proved suppliers; they do not assume positivity or irreducibility of cell modules. The generic Schur element $c_E(v)$ is determined by $\tau_K=\sum_Ec_E(v)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_E$. Its lowest term will be proved to be $f_Ev^{-2\alpha_E}$ with $f_E$ a positive integer. A specialization $\theta:A\to k$ has $u=\theta(v)\in k^\times$, multiplicative parameter $\xi=u^2$, and is **L-good** when $\theta(f_E)\ne0$ for every generic label $E$. Characteristic zero is always L-good. The modular theorem does not require $\theta(c_E(v))\ne0$.

To compare normalizations, Geck's multiplicative generator is $S_s=v^{L(s)}T_s$ and obeys $(S_s-v^{2L(s)})(S_s+1)=0$; after specialization its parameter is $\xi^{L(s)}$. The asymptotic formulas below use Lusztig's revised convention $D_w\leftrightarrow t_w$ and coefficients $n_d$ in $\phi$, with no diagonal sign change. Geck's signed starred convention is not mixed into these formulas.
thm-unequal-parameter-cell-quotients-are:
## Statement

For every Coxeter system and weight function of [[def-unequal-parameter-coxeter-hecke-algebra]], the spans $I^L_{\le\mathcal C}$ and $I^L_{<\mathcal C}$ attached to a left cell are left ideals; the right-cell spans are right ideals; and the two-sided-cell spans are two-sided ideals. Therefore the quotients defined in [[def-unequal-parameter-cells-and-cell-quotients]] are left modules, right modules, or bimodules, respectively. Each quotient has an $A$-basis consisting exactly of the images of the KL basis elements indexed by its cell. No further cell property, semisimplicity, or irreducible-module classification is asserted.
lem-lusztig-asymptotic-algebra-and-speci:
## Statement

Assume [[def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data]], including P2–P8 and P15′. The free abelian group $J=\bigoplus_{w\in W}\mathbb Zt_w$ is an associative algebra under $t_xt_y=\sum_z\gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}}t_z$, with identity $\sum_{d\in\mathcal D}n_dt_d$. It has an anti-involution $\iota_J(t_w)=t_{w^{-1}}$ and a perfect symmetrizing trace $\mu(t_w)=n_w$ for $w\in\mathcal D$ and zero otherwise, with $\mu(t_xt_y)=\delta_{x,y^{-1}}$.

Put $J^i=\langle t_w:a(w)=i\rangle_{\mathbb Z}$ and $I_i=\langle D_w:a(w)\ge i\rangle_A$, and $B_i=I_i/I_{i+1}$. These are respectively mutually orthogonal two-sided ideals of $J$, two-sided ideals of $H$, and free layers on the classes $[D_w]$ with $a(w)=i$. The identification $[D_w]\mapsto t_w$ makes $B_i$ a left $J_A$-module and a $(J_A,H)$-bimodule. The map

$$\phi:H\longrightarrow J_A,\qquad \phi(D_x)=\sum_{\substack{z\in W,\ d\in\mathcal D\\a(z)=a(d)}}h_{x,d,z}n_dt_z$$

is a unital algebra homomorphism, and the natural left $H$ action on $B_i$ is exactly restriction along $\phi$. Here the sum means $z\in W,d\in\mathcal D$.

All these statements survive any commutative coefficient specialization. With $N=\max_wa(w)$, $(\ker\phi_R)^{N+1}=0$ for every specialization to a field or ring $R$. Over $K=\mathbb Q(v)$, $\phi_K$ is an isomorphism. The rational algebra $J_{\mathbb Q}$ is split semisimple. Its simple modules $V_E$ can be indexed by the generic labels $E$ so that $K\otimes V_E$, restricted through $\phi_K$, is $E$. Each has a unique support degree $\alpha_E$ such that $J^{\alpha_E}_{\mathbb Q}V_E=V_E$ and the other $J^i$ act by zero.
thm-a1xa1-unequal-parameter-cells-give-a:
## Statement

Let $W=\langle s,t\mid s^2=t^2=1,\ (st)^2=1\rangle$, the finite Weyl group $A_1\times A_1$, and let $L(s)=1,\ L(t)=2$. Form its weighted Hecke algebra with coefficient $v$ and the symmetric quadratic convention $(T_r-v^{L(r)})(T_r+v^{-L(r)})=0$. Let $O=\mathbb Z_p$ for an odd prime $p$, let $q=1+p$, and specialize $v\mapsto q$. Write $K=\mathbb Q_p$, $k=\mathbb F_p$, and let $D$ be the decomposition matrix of the four explicit $O$-lattices obtained from the cell quotients.

The left, right, and two-sided cells are the four singleton sets $\{1\},\{s\},\{t\},\{st\}$. Their four cell modules are pairwise distinct one-dimensional $K$-modules, and each has an $O$-stable rank-one lattice. Their reductions are the four distinct simple $H_k$-modules, so $D$ is the $4\times4$ identity matrix up to the displayed ordering. Consequently, relative to any integer-valued statistic $\alpha$ on the generic simple modules, these four cell modules form a canonical basic set in the sense of [[def-canonical-basic-set-for-hecke-specialization]].

This is a finite Weyl case. In Geck's normalization, its specialization also satisfies the exact hypothesis $\theta(c_\chi)\ne0$ for every generic irreducible character in Theorem 4.11; the proof below verifies the decomposition matrix directly.
lem-schur-leading-coefficients-and-good-:
## Statement

Use the data and hypotheses of [[def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data]]. For each rational simple $J_{\mathbb Q}$-module $V_E$ supplied by [[lem-lusztig-asymptotic-algebra-and-specialization-map]], let $\chi_E^J$ be its character and $\alpha_E$ its support degree. There are positive integers $f_E$ such that

$$\mu_{\mathbb Q}=\sum_Ef_E^{-1}\chi_E^J,\qquad c_E(v)=f_Ev^{-2\alpha_E}+\text{strictly higher powers of }v.$$

Thus $\alpha_E$ is precisely the Schur-element exponent in Geck's convention. The full Schur elements $c_E(v)$ lie in $A$. Each $V_E$ has a full finite free $J$-stable integral lattice $\Lambda_E$. Put $F=\prod_Ef_E$ and $S=\mathbb Z[1/F]$. There is an explicit algebra isomorphism

$$J_S\ \cong\ \prod_E\operatorname{End}_S(S\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\Lambda_E).$$

Consequently, for every field $k$ of characteristic zero or characteristic not dividing any $f_E$, the algebra $J_k$ is split semisimple with simple modules $V_{E,k}=k\otimes\Lambda_E$, preserving dimensions and support degrees. More generally the displayed matrix decomposition holds after base change to any commutative ring in which every $f_E$ is a unit. The actual Hecke model is already free globally: $L_{E,A}=A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\Lambda_E$, with $H_A$ acting through the integral map $\phi_A$ and the integral $J$-matrices. Its generic fibre is $E$, and every local model used below is the base change of this displayed free module. No assertion that arbitrary torsion-free lattices over higher-dimensional local rings are free is used. No hypothesis that every specialized full Schur element $\theta(c_E(v))$ is nonzero is imposed.
lem-asymptotic-induction-identifies-lead:
## Statement

In the finite-Weyl setting of [[def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data]], assume its specified Lusztig properties and let $\theta:A\to k$ have characteristic zero or satisfy $\theta(f_E)\ne0$ for every generic simple label $E$. Write $H=H_k$, and let $V_E$ be the corresponding simple module of the split asymptotic algebra $J_k$, supported in degree $\alpha_E$. A star denotes restriction through $\phi_k:H\to J_k$.

For each simple $H$-module $M$, let $a_M=\max\{a(w):D_wM\ne0\}$, where $D_w=C_w^\dagger$. There is an injective assignment $M\mapsto E(M)$ such that $\alpha_{E(M)}=a_M$, $M$ occurs once in $*V_{E(M)}$, and all its other simple factors have strictly smaller $a$-value. Moreover $H$ is split: every simple $H$-module remains simple over every field extension.
lem-filtered-projectives-prove-canonical:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the finite-Weyl data and Lusztig properties of [[def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data]]. Let $\theta:A\to k$ have characteristic zero or $\theta(f_E)\ne0$ for every generic simple label $E$. Put $k_0=\operatorname{Frac}(\theta(A))\subseteq k$, let $R=\widehat{A_{\ker\theta}}$, and let $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$. Take the explicit global free model $L_{E,A}=A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\Lambda_E$ of the Schur supplier, whose Hecke matrices are integral because the $J$-matrices and $\phi_A$ are integral. Let $L_E=R\otimes_A L_{E,A}$. This is the standard free module of the $E$-matrix block of $J_R$, restricted through $\phi_R$; its freeness is by this construction, not an inference from torsion-freeness over $R$. Its fraction fibre is the generic simple $E_F$; its residue is the restricted asymptotic simple $*V_E$. Define
$$
d_{E,M}=[k\otimes_{k_0}(L_E/\mathfrak m_RL_E):M]
$$
for simple $H_k$-modules $M$. These multiplicities agree with those of any other free stable $R$-models of the same generic simples. They are unchanged by extension from $k_0$ to $k$, using the simple-label bijection.

For a simple $H_k$-module $M$, choose an idempotent $e\in H_k$ such that $H_ke$ is its projective cover. Regarding the layers $B_i=I_i/I_{i+1}$ as left $J_k$-modules and right $H_k$-modules, one has
$$
\operatorname{mult}_{J_k}(V_E,B_ie)=\begin{cases}d_{E,M},&i=\alpha_E,\\0,&i\ne\alpha_E.\end{cases}
$$
Moreover $d_{E,M}=[*V_E:M]$. No identification of the right action on $B_i$ with right multiplication by $\phi_k$ is assumed.
thm-finite-weyl-canonical-basic-sets-fro:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with integral nonnegative weight function $L$, and impose exactly the generic splitting and Lusztig properties specified in [[def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data]], namely P2–P8 and P15′. Let $H_A$ be its Hecke algebra over $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$. For every unital specialization $\theta:A\to k$ into a field, assume that $k$ has characteristic zero or that every leading Schur integer $f_E$ is nonzero in $k$. Write the generic Schur element as $c_E=f_Ev^{-2\alpha_E}$ plus terms of strictly higher $v$-degree.

Then $H_k$ is split and has a unique canonical basic set for the decomposition matrix $d_{E,M}$ furnished by the free asymptotic models in [[lem-filtered-projectives-prove-canonical-basic-set-reciprocity]]. Explicitly, there is an injection $M\mapsto E(M)$ from simple $H_k$-labels to generic labels, with
$$
d_{E(M),M}=1,\qquad \alpha_{E(M)}=\min\{\alpha_E:d_{E,M}>0\},
$$
and
$$
d_{E,M}>0\ \Longrightarrow\ E=E(M)\ \text{or}\ \alpha_E>\alpha_{E(M)}.
$$
Its image is the canonical basic set of [[def-canonical-basic-set-for-hecke-specialization]]. In normalized generators the parameters are $\theta(v)^{L(s)}$; in Geck's multiplicative generators they are $\theta(v^2)^{L(s)}$. No condition $\theta(c_E)\ne0$ is imposed: nonsemisimple specializations are included. The Lusztig properties here are hypotheses, not universal assertions for all unequal weights or all Coxeter groups.
cor-weighted-cell-quotients-and-finite-w:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-finite-weyl-canonical-basic-sets-from-lusztig-properties]], the function $a$ is constant on every left, right and two-sided weighted cell. Each $a$-layer of the KL cell filtration has a finite filtration with cell quotients. For the dagger basis $D_w=C_w^\dagger$, these quotients are the dagger twists of the native cell modules of [[def-unequal-parameter-cells-and-cell-quotients]]: on the twist, $h$ acts as $h^\dagger$ on the original module.

Every generic simple $E$ occurs in a dagger-twisted left cell module with cell $a$-value $\alpha_E$, and every generic constituent of such a module has that same Schur exponent. For each specialized simple $M$, its canonical basic-set label $E(M)$ occurs in a dagger-twisted generic left cell module of $a$-value $a_M=\alpha_{E(M)}$, whose specialization contains $M$. In that specialization the contribution from $E(M)$ has multiplicity one per generic copy, and every other generic label contributing to $M$ has strictly larger Schur exponent; hence no other generic label of that same cell $a$-value contributes to $M$.

This is a general finite-Weyl cell/basic-set connection, including nonsemisimple fibers. It does not assert that every cell module is simple or that cells themselves are in bijection with special simples.
